chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

He said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the Throne in quarters. He did not create anything before it except three things: the Air, the Pen, and the Light. Then He created it from different lights: among them is green light that made greenness, yellow light that made yellowness, red light that made redness, and white light, which is the light of all lights, from which is made the light of day. Then He made it into seventy thousand layers, the thickness of each layer being like the first layer of the Throne down to the lowest of the low. There is no layer among them that does not glorify its Lord with praise and sanctify Him with different sounds and distinct tongues. If He allowed the tongue of one of them to be heard, and something of what is beneath it were heard, it would destroy the mountains, cities, and fortresses, and swallow the seas, and destroy what is below it. It has eight pillars, on each of which are angels whose number only Allah, the Mighty and High, knows. They glorify Him night and day without ceasing. If anything of what is above it were sensed, it would not stand for the blink of an eye. Between it and the sensing are omnipotence, magnificence, greatness, holiness, and mercy, then knowledge. And there is no word beyond this.
The chapter explaining the meaning of Allah's statement: 'His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth.'

key_terms.السَّافِلِينَ: The lowest of the low (depths of the earth)
key_terms.الطَّبَق: Layer or stratum of the Throne
key_terms.الْعَرْش: The Throne, the highest creation of God
key_terms.الْقَلَم: The Pen, used to record divine decree
key_terms.الْكُرْسِي: The Footstool or Seat of Divine Knowledge

ai.seo_question: What is the structure and composition of the Throne (Al-Arsh) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this cosmological narrative to illustrate the immense scale and luminous composition of the Al-Arsh, emphasizing its pre-existence alongside the Pen and Light as foundational divine creations. The description of seventy thousand layers and distinct angelic choirs serves to highlight the sensory magnitude of the divine realm, bridging metaphysical theology with the Quranic concept of the Kursi's all-encompassing nature.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar, on the authority of `Ali ibn Isma`il, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn `Umar al-Yamani, on the authority of Abu al-Tafayl, on the authority of Abu Ja`far that `Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the Throne in quarters. He did not create anything before except three things: the Air, the Pen, and the Light. Then He created the Throne from different lights: then from the Light, He created green light that made greenness, yellow light that made yellowness, red light that made redness, and white light, which is the light of all lights from which is made day light. He then made the Throne of seventy thousand thick layers. Each layer is like the first throne to the lower one. There is not a throne that does not exalt and glorify its Lord with praise with different sounds, and in different language. The sounds of the tongues are so loud that if He wished them to be heard, they would destroy the mountains, cities, and strongholds of the earth; the oceans would overtake the land, destroying everything but itself. The Throne has eight pillars. Each pillar has angels whose numbers is unknown to all but Allah, the Mighty and High, and who exalt Him day and night without subsiding. If anything were sensed of it, but what is above it, it will not stand for the blink of an eye between it, and the sense of the omnipotence, the magnificence, the sublimity, the glorification, the mercy, and then the knowledge. And there is no word to describe what exists beyond this.
